title: Accessing an association proxy in an after_flush context duplicates the last linked object

labels.name: unit of work
labels.description: the persistence phase within the ORM.

body:
Hello,

When writing some after_flush code we noticed a strange behavior, where the last linked child object is duplicated in the parent object's association proxy. This association proxy is a many to many.

Here's a little script to reproduce

```python
import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.ext.associationproxy import association_proxy

engine = sa.create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:')
Base = declarative_base()
Base.metadata.bind = engine
Session = sa.orm.sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
session = sa.orm.scoped_session(Session)


class Teacher(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'teacher'
    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)


class Class(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'class'

    teacher = sa.orm.relationship('Teacher', backref='classes')
    teacher_id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, sa.ForeignKey('teacher.id'), primary_key=True)

    student = sa.orm.relationship('Student', backref='classes')
    student_id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, sa.ForeignKey('student.id'), primary_key=True)


class Student(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'student'

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)

    teachers = association_proxy('classes', 'teacher')



@sa.event.listens_for(Session, 'after_flush')
def report_teachers(session, flush_context):
    for target in set(session.new).union(session.dirty):
        if isinstance(target, Student):
            print(target.teachers)
            print([t.id for t in target.teachers])

Base.metadata.create_all()

student = Student()

french_class = Class(teacher=Teacher(), student=student)
session.add(french_class)
session.commit()

dutch_class = Class(teacher=Teacher(), student=student)
session.add(dutch_class)
session.commit()
```

When running this script, the result is 

```
❱ python test.py
[<__main__.Teacher object at 0x7f6df50bb6d8>]
[1]
[<__main__.Teacher object at 0x7f6df5048cf8>, <__main__.Teacher object at 0x7f6df5048da0>, <__main__.Teacher object at 0x7f6df5088978>]
[1, 2, 2]
```

As you can see, after the first commit, the list only has the teacher for the french class, while after the second commit, the list has one teacher for the french class, and a duplicated teacher for the dutch class (same database id, different internal python id).

Doing a `session.refresh(target)` within the after flush is a current workaround.

Versions this was reproduced on:
- 1.2.0b3
- current master branch (3836a90dcf9b202db2eb8f013b8eca07245067be)

Python version is 3.6.7

To allow Mr. Bayer's fun on Link's awakening, I will investigate further and see if I can propose a fix at a later date ;)
